title: Identifiable Return in Memristive Associative Memory: A Generative Collapse Dynamics Analysis of Recurrent Pattern Completion
lens: identity-aware retrospective return audit of an external hardware experiment
object_of_study: Identity-preserving recurrent pattern completion under declared cue corruption and hardware constraints.
main_question: Under what conditions does a physically constrained recurrent computation recover the intended memory rather than merely settle, repeat, or produce a similar state?

claim_layers.claim: He et al. (SRC-000051, Nature Communications 17, 3096, 2026) report a hardware-adaptive learning algorithm for associative memory on memristor crossbars with released trajectory data (as read by the local analysis).

The local manuscript (SRC-000052, Version 1.2) supplies an identity-aware recovery certificate, a reproducible retrospective audit of ten released trajectories, target-specific acceptance regions, a reconstruction residual, local contraction, an implementation-error burden, separation from competing memories, and a prospective test design.

Version 1.2 boundary: the analysis includes a retrospective evidence freeze and acquired Figure-3 arrays; it does not retroactively become preregistered; no new chip experiment, completed hardware certificate, or completed UMCP kernel run is claimed.
The library places this as external ingress with diagnostic and domain-translation secondary roles; no GCD interpretation is attributed to He et al.
